observations: Fail-closed, as the spec asks, in every unreadable shape: a typed Go constant (`maxInputChars int = 32000`), a top-level `const maxInputChars = 32000` outside the const block, hexadecimal, digit separators, an arithmetic expression, a missing semicolon and a trailing `/* */` all refuse rather than pass. The refusal names the file and prints the pattern it needs, which shows exactly what is wrong even where its enumeration (`digit separators, hexadecimal, an expression`) does not name the shape — a `const` keyword or a block-comment trailer on the declaration line. None of these is a defect: no input in 17 trees made the check pass when it should have failed.

A file present but unreadable (mode 000) ends the check with a Python PermissionError traceback and exit 1, where a missing file and a non-UTF-8 file each give a clean `::error file=…` line (the suite pins both). It still fails closed, and a checkout never produces it, so this is noted rather than filed.

The check's soundness premises were read rather than assumed: the comment and message triggers enqueue `new.body` alone (store/migrations/0075_comments_embeddings_trigger.up.sql:6, 0077_messages_embeddings_trigger.up.sql:10) and the backfill selects the same column (embedqueue/queue.go:724, :732), so nothing is prepended to the text whose length the body cap bounds; embed.go:174 truncates with text.HeadRunes(t, maxInputChars) and embed_test.go:138-144 pins that the truncated text has exactly maxInputChars runes, so the rune-versus-UTF-16 argument the equality rests on is itself locked by an existing Go test.
